I have been farming these same 3 mu for 18 years, so I mostly do what worked last year. My husband works in town part of the year, so I handle most of the field work myself with help from my mother-in-law at busy times.

I split my land like this: about 2 mu for wheat-maize rotation, and 1 mu for cotton. Cotton still brings good cash if the price holds, and I have grown it since I married into this village.

For wheat, I plant Jimai variety — the seed dealer in town sells it and my neighbor Wang had 480 kg last year with it. I put 2 bags of compound fertilizer (about 40 kg of 15-15-15) as base before sowing, and then topdress urea around March when it greens up, maybe 15 kg. I irrigate with the well — once before winter, once at jointing, once at filling. Three times is enough if rain comes in May. I spray once for aphids, sometimes twice if I see them bad.

For maize after wheat, I plant Zhengdan hybrid seed, everyone around here does. I put one bag of compound fertilizer at sowing and then 20 kg urea at the big trumpet stage. Maize is thirsty, I water twice from the well. One spray for corn borer is usually enough.

Cotton is the most work. I use hybrid Bt seed — saves me spraying for bollworm, though I still spray 3-4 times for aphids and mites. I put heavy base fertilizer, about 50 kg compound plus 15 kg urea topdressed at flowering, and extra potassium because cotton needs it for the bolls. I irrigate 3-4 times because cotton can't take drought at flowering.

I plough before wheat and cotton, but for summer maize I just use rotary tillage after wheat harvest — no time to plough, maize must go in fast.
